questions.q: Why do duplicate party records tend to happen in HZ_PARTIES?
options: HZ_PARTIES automatically merges identical companies, so duplicates are impossible
Because parties are entered by people, the same real-world company can be entered more than once with slightly different names or addresses
Because HZ_PARTIES only stores one row per customer by design
Because duplicate parties are generated automatically by Subledger Accounting
questions.explain: Manual, inconsistent data entry (e.g. "Acme Corp" vs. "Acme Corporation") is the classic source of duplicate party records in Trading Community Architecture.

questions.q: What does an XLA_EVENTS row with no corresponding XLA_AE_HEADERS row usually indicate?
options: A duplicate supplier record
A period that is permanently closed
A normal, healthy transaction
A configuration gap — the accounting rules or mapping didn't produce a journal entry for that event
questions.explain: A stuck transaction (validated but never accounted) typically points to a mapping/configuration issue, not a performance delay.

questions.q: Why is summing ENTERED_DR/ENTERED_CR across transactions in different currencies risky?
options: It produces a total that looks plausible but is meaningless, because the amounts aren't actually in the same currency unit
ENTERED_DR and ENTERED_CR don't exist on GL_JE_LINES
It only affects Receivables, never Payables
It isn't risky — entered amounts are always directly comparable
questions.explain: Entered amounts are in each transaction's own currency; mixing them across currencies without converting produces a quietly wrong total.

Troubleshooting Oracle Financials
